Does anybody know why the weights start out random instead of all zero?
212

@petra.k

1 year ago
If every weight starts at zero, every neuron in a layer computes exactly the same thing and gets exactly the same update, so they stay identical forever and the whole layer behaves like a single neuron. Random starting values break that symmetry. They are kept small so that the early outputs do not saturate, and there are standard recipes for how small, depending on the activation function you use and on how many inputs feed each neuron.
